Málaga demonstrates three materially different urban-beach contexts inside one city: central civic/tourism foreground, traditional promenade/fishing barrio, and active maritime-neighborhood beach edge.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Initial portfolio reconciliation from the seven supplied settlement packages and supplied portfolio overview; no external research performed.
notes: Shared families are preliminary research candidates.
The supplied overview’s warning that coastal cities are not one archetype is preserved by keeping strong city variants and unresolved notes.
City files remain primary research authority; this portfolio file is derived comparison only.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Torrevieja city-reviewed evidence against the Phase 1 seven-city portfolio. Existing shared structural families were refined; no new shared geometry family was forced after only one Phase 2 city pass.
notes: Torrevieja low-rise-compound remains city-specific/provisional pending equivalent re-research in other cities.
Molino del Agua was removed from the generic urban-park family after official evidence confirmed protected dune-and-pine landscape character.
Port/harbor stays in a shared POI classification family while its geometry/treatment remains explicitly unique.
Shared families remain derived recommendations; Torrevieja city file is the primary authority.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Elche city-reviewed evidence against the current seven-city portfolio after the Torrevieja review. Existing structural families were refined and Elche gained a narrow detached-garden member; no shared POI family was created for the unique Palmeral cultural landscape or La Calahorra.
notes: Elche Palmeral remains a unique city-defining landscape/spatial-grammar authority rather than being forced into the generic urban-park POI family.
Ciudad Jardín now contributes a specific detached-garden member to the shared Mediterranean detached-house archetype; the broader Elche rowhouse/villa family remains separate.
Los Palmerales remains inside the shared open-block structural archetype but requires an explicit city-specific public-housing facade/massing variant.
Arenales strengthens the shared coastal-apartment family, while La Marina is explicitly constrained against continuous resort morphology.
The unique Alicante–Elche passenger terminal is separated from reusable airport support typologies.
Shared families remain derived recommendations; the Elche city file is the primary authority.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Alicante Phase 2 findings after Torrevieja and Elche reviews. Refined existing shared archetypes rather than creating city-name-based duplicates; added Postiguet to the shared urban-beach POI family.
notes: Open-block family gains documented Virgen del Remedio and Juan XXIII city-specific subprofiles under the shared slab/estate archetype.
Historic attached family gains Nueva Tabarca traditional house as a city-specific island profile under the shared attached-finegrain structure.
Port family is refined with Alicante passenger/city-facing versus operational/logistics distinction.
Industrial family is refined with multi-area and Mercalicante campus/site grammar.
Coastal tower family preserves future-state guardrails for Nueva Albufereta and PAU 5.
Playa del Postiguet is added to the shared urban-beach POI family; Explanada remains city-specific pending later cross-city waterfront reconciliation.
Shared families remain derived recommendations; the Alicante city file is the primary authority.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Benidorm Phase 2 after Torrevieja, Elche and Alicante reviews. The shared coastal tower archetype is retained only at structural level; Benidorm’s open-plot/communal-landscape grammar is explicitly strengthened as a city variant, while hotel/podium/new-compound tower families remain separate. Added Benidorm’s three principal urban beaches to the shared beach POI classification.
notes: Benidorm demonstrates why a city cannot be represented by a high-rise palette swap: tower footprint, parcel scale, spacing, communal landscape and waterfront relationship matter alongside height.
Poniente and Levante require different site grammar despite both supporting tall buildings.
Paseo de Poniente and Serra Gelada remain city-specific/place-specific authorities rather than being forced into new generic cross-city POI families at this stage.
Intempo, Gran Hotel Bali and Town Hall remain unique bespoke candidates; they are not shared-family members.
Shared families remain derived recommendations; the Benidorm city file is primary research authority.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Cartagena after city review: refined historic, Ensanche, port, industrial and coastal variants; added a source-supported historic peripheral-house member to the shared low-rise row/townhouse family; added two Mar Menor beach POIs. No new cross-city structural family was created solely from Cartagena.
notes: Unique Modernista buildings, Roman Theatre/Museum, ARQVA, El Batel, Cabo lighthouse, naval/shipyard and Escombreras heavy-industry remain city-specific/unique authorities rather than forced shared families.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Málaga after city review: added La Palmilla walk-up to shared open-block/estate archetype, strengthened eastern villa/coastal variants, refined TechPark/industrial/port/airport variants, added Málaga urban-beach variants, replaced protected Guadalhorce estuary with Parque de Málaga in the urban-park family, and left Avenida de Andalucía tower-on-podium as city-specific pending cross-city comparison.
notes: No new cross-city structural family was created solely from Málaga.
Avenida de Andalucía tower-on-podium remains a Málaga city-specific profile candidate until comparable arterial tower/podium evidence is reviewed elsewhere.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Reconciled Murcia after city review: split Vistabella/La Paz/La Fama estate subtypes from broad baseline families; narrowed pedanía versus huerta/resort grammar; refined institutional, industrial and airport variants; added unique civic/heritage and landscape anchors. This completes Phase 2 city review coverage for all seven settlements without creating a new cross-city structural family solely from Murcia.
notes: No new cross-city structural family is created solely from Murcia.
The shared low-rise row/townhouse family no longer contains Murcia resort housing pending resort-specific structural sampling.
Murcia Phase 2 completes the 7/7 city re-research sequence; all shared-family conclusions remain research recommendations rather than production decisions.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Seven-city Phase 2 closeout reconciliation after all city reviews. Stable shared-family IDs and memberships are retained from the Murcia-carried final index; stale pre-review wording is resolved, the airport family label is clarified to ancillary/support fabric, and no new shared structural or POI family is created.
notes: No city catalog research conclusion is overwritten by this portfolio closeout.
Shared-family conclusions remain research recommendations, not production implementation decisions.
Named passenger terminals remain bespoke authorities despite the stable legacy family ID arch-airport-terminal-support.
Historical reconciliation entries are preserved verbatim even where their field naming reflects an evolving convention.

reconciliationHistory.summary: Applied completed Phase 3 exception research P3-001, P3-003, P3-004 and P3-005. Existing shared-family memberships are retained; refinements strengthen city/zone site grammar and narrow the semantic use of broad city records without creating a new shared family.
notes: No stable shared-family ID was renamed or removed.
No new shared building family or shared POI family was created.
Four independent Phase 3 exceptions now support a deferred future schema distinction between structural family and site/development grammar; no schema migration is applied in this handover.
